symptom: Pasting a local file from a Windows clipboard can produce a malformed path when a file URI is decoded on a Windows host, while POSIX file URIs must remain valid on every host.
direct_cause: The shared clipboard parser delegated file URI pathname conversion to the host-specific fileURLToPath helper, which interprets a POSIX URI pathname differently on Windows and can manufacture an invalid drive-prefixed path.
class_root: Clipboard payloads are a cross-platform protocol boundary, but URI paths, drive paths, UNC paths, and native multi-string paths were not normalized according to their protocol form before entering the local asset pipeline.
affected_population: Windows users pasting files copied by applications that expose public.file-url or text/uri-list
Users pasting UNC-shared files from a Windows clipboard
POSIX users receiving drive-qualified or URI-form clipboard payloads
entry_points: parseClipboardFilePaths for public.file-url, text/uri-list, and text/plain URI payloads
parseClipboardFilePaths for FileNameW and FileName native Windows payloads

external_sources.purpose: Confirm file URI drive-letter, authority, localhost, and local POSIX path forms are protocol syntax independent of the host implementation.
Confirm Windows clipboard has native file-list formats distinct from URI text formats.

invariants: A file URI is decoded according to URI syntax first; only drive-qualified and UNC forms are converted to host Windows separators.
A local POSIX file URI remains an absolute POSIX path even when the parser runs on Windows.
Native FileNameW/FileName values are accepted only when they are absolute paths and are deduplicated before import.

recurrence.reason: Every Windows, POSIX, URI-list, or native clipboard paste can reach the same protocol-to-host path boundary, so host-dependent parsing could repeatedly corrupt equivalent payloads.
same_class_scan: Scanned all parseClipboardFilePaths callers and clipboard format branches for URI, FileNameW, FileName, and plain-text path inputs.
Scanned downstream asset import guards to confirm path existence and media validation remain owned after protocol normalization.
Exercised Windows drive, UNC authority, localhost, POSIX absolute, multi-string, malformed URI, and duplicate payload boundaries.

prevention.strategy: Normalize clipboard payloads by protocol form before applying host-specific separators or passing paths to the asset pipeline.

migration: Clipboard payloads are transient and have no stored schema. Existing imported assets retain their persisted local path; the corrected parser applies to the next paste without rewriting stored assets.
residual_risks: A clipboard producer that emits a malformed URI remains rejected rather than repaired heuristically.
The parser does not verify that a returned path exists; the downstream local asset import boundary remains responsible for file availability and media validation.
